reader.requirement: At --std 85 every separately compiled program in a sequence of programs submitted together must end with an END PROGRAM header except the last, so the compiler must refuse a program that precedes another without one and accept the last program with or without one.

edition-consulted.switches: where a CONTAINED program may stand (after the procedure division from 2002); not the separately-compiled sequence this rule governs

reader.edition-search: EndMarkerPass consults the EditionContext only to report; grep Edition|Version|Construct in EndMarkerPass.cs and SourceUnitShape.cs: the SR1 positional check (precedesAnother) is the same code at every edition.
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_f05_01 is one well-formed sequence; the refusal of a non-last program without END PROGRAM and a three-program sequence are not exercised

probes.printed: error COBOL2793: PROGRAM-ID 'PROGA' precedes another source unit, so its end marker END PROGRAM PROGA shall be present (ISO §2023:10.7.3 SR1)
probes.expected: refused: PROGA is not the last program and has no end program header
accepted: the last program may omit the end program header
accepted: the last program may also carry one (the format brackets it)

probes.printed: error COBOL2793: PROGRAM-ID 'PROGB' precedes another source unit ...
probes.expected: refused: the middle program of three lacks its end program header

citations.check: OK  §1985:VI.2.3.3 GR2  (2.3.3 General Rules)  the text is in GR2

reader.notes: EndMarkerPass.ScreenProgram's SR1 arm reports a program definition that precedes another unit of the compilation group without an end marker; at 85 it fires exactly where the 1985 rule requires. The diagnostic cites §2023:10.7.3 SR1 rather than the 1985 rule even at --std 85, a message-text matter, not a conformance failure.

refuter.evidence: refute-1985-189/seq5.cob: PROGA with END PROGRAM, a comment line, then PROGB containing PROGC (both END PROGRAM), then a last PROGD with none -> compiles and prints IN PROGA / IN PROGB / IN PROGC / IN PROGD. seq6.cob: PROGA with no END PROGRAM followed by PROGN and PROGZ (each with END PROGRAM) -> refused COBOL2793 at (2,8); both readings (PROGA a non-last separately compiled program, or a container) require its header. With the reader's seq1..seq4 the positional rule fires exactly on every program but the last. The diagnostic cites §2023:10.7.3 SR1 at --std 85, a message-text matter, not the behaviour. cite.py: OK  §1985:VI.2.3.3 GR2  (2.3.3 General Rules)  the text is in GR2.
